## S5 control

Task 6. Date 2026-10-11 (runs 20:05 to 20:12 UTC). Main checkout `/Users/jedaisaboteur/Repositories/getwrite`, branch `feat/two-client-save-measurement`, `git rev-parse --short HEAD` = `b9d08ced` (the new script `scripts/s5-control.mjs` and `results/s5/` are new, uncommitted files under `specs/`). `node --version` = `v24.15.0` (no Node 22 or Node 20 run is claimed). Script: `scripts/s5-control.mjs` (written in this task; it uses the Task 2 harness libraries unchanged; the per-project file hashing helper is inside the script, not in `lib/`). Result JSON: `results/s5/s5v<variant>r<n>-<run id>-rep0<n>.json` (9 files), per-repetition digests `results/s5/<run id>-rep0<n>-digest.txt` (9 files), `results/s5/summary-s5v1r1-mv495jtw-2e7e94.json`.

**THIS IS A CONTROL.** Two clients, two DIFFERENT resources (R1 and R2) in ONE project, one client per resource. It is here so that any interference between resources can be told apart from interference between two clients of the same resource. Any interference found in this section would be interference between resources and is the first thing to read when S1 to S4 or S2 show something odd. (None was found in these 9 repetitions; see the verdicts.) It says nothing about two clients saving the SAME resource: that is S1 to S4 and S2.

**Server (every repetition): the built standalone server** (`frontend/.next/standalone/frontend/server.js`, built at `812f2859` in Task 1, reused; `frontend/` unchanged, so not rebuilt), sharing on, on a free port the script picked, one fresh server, one fresh project and two fresh resources per repetition. **Every request in this section is host to itself (the private LAN address of this machine), not a second-device result.** Both clients are headless Chromium (Playwright `chrome-headless-shell`), two separate paired browser contexts, real keystrokes into the TipTap editor.

### Where each thing ran

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| `node --check scripts/s5-control.mjs`, `pnpm knip`, `git status` | inside the command sandbox |
| the 9 repetitions (`node scripts/s5-control.mjs 1,2,3 3`), the throwaway servers, Chromium, every `lsof` / `ps` check, and the read-only python aggregation of the result JSON | OUTSIDE the sandbox (`dangerouslyDisableSandbox`) |

Output of the run: `/tmp/getwrite-two-client/logs/s5-run1.out` (the full printed records, request logs as long JSON lines, not pasted whole). Server logs: `/tmp/getwrite-two-client/logs/s5v<variant>r<n>-<run id>-server.log` (not read, not pasted).

### What was run (3 timing variants, 3 repetitions each, 9 repetitions in all, every one recorded, none discarded)

Sequence of one repetition: a fresh server, project and two text resources R1 and R2, each holding the base document `BASE alpha bravo charlie` (the two base documents were byte-identical). The stores of both resources and a sha256 of every file in the project are taken (the "before"). Client A opens R1, client B opens R2 (each in the real editor; footers `All changes saved · not saved yet`), the project is settled and hashed again. A types ` A1` into R1 and B types ` B1` into R2 with real keystrokes (caret to the end with `ControlOrMeta+End`, 40 ms per key, about 140 ms from first to last key). Each client's own 2500 ms debounce (read, not run: `useCanonicalAutosave.ts`) produces its save. The timing variants differ in when the two saves are SENT:

| Variant | How the two saves are timed | Asked |
|---|---|---|
| 1 in turn | A types and waits for saved; B starts typing 5 s after A's acknowledgement (stores of both resources read, hashed, in between); no hold | 5000 ms from A's acknowledgement to B's first key |
| 2 smallest gap | both clients type at once (`Promise.all` of the two typings); both PATCHes are held in Playwright route handlers; the two releases are issued in the same tick (`Promise.all` of the two `releaseHeld` calls) | 0 ms: the smallest gap this harness can produce |
| 3 250 ms gap | the same, but A's PATCH is released, the script sleeps 250 ms, then B's is released | 250 ms |

Then: quiet wait and read of both resources, hash; 30 s after the last acknowledgement both editors are read without a reload; both clients reload and reopen their own resource; quiet wait, read, hash. The held-request footer reads `Saving…` on both clients while held (an artefact of holding the request, seen in the Task 2 hold check too).

**Achieved gaps (measured from the logged times; no pair is called simultaneous without its gap).** Times are Playwright event times on the host clock, not wire times. "Effective send" is the release time for a held request (the moment the harness continued it) and the page's request event otherwise. B minus A, in ms:


| Rep (run id) | Effective-send gap | Request-event gap | Response-arrival gap | Response `updatedAt` gap | Held before release (A / B) | First to be sent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1 rep 1 (`s5v1r1-mv495jtw-2e7e94`) | 7695.213 | 7695.213 | 7696.450 | 7697 | - / - | A |
| v1 rep 2 (`s5v1r2-mv496qpx-2db6f5`) | 7731.002 | 7731.002 | 7728.843 | 7729 | - / - | A |
| v1 rep 3 (`s5v1r3-mv497xda-eb5d39`) | 7719.484 | 7719.484 | 7716.258 | 7716 | - / - | A |
| v2 rep 1 (`s5v2r1-mv49940j-7ee9c2`) | 0.563 | 0.635 | -1.147 | -1 | 336 / 336 | A |
| v2 rep 2 (`s5v2r2-mv49a52d-ea1310`) | 0.162 | -0.823 | -1.221 | -1 | 322 / 323 | A |
| v2 rep 3 (`s5v2r3-mv49b66r-3104ba`) | 0.231 | -0.754 | 0.937 | 1 | 330 / 331 | A |
| v3 rep 1 (`s5v3r1-mv49c7au-aa8258`) | 253.125 | 0.765 | 247.717 | 249 | 332 / 584 | A |
| v3 rep 2 (`s5v3r2-mv49d8la-0e194b`) | 252.732 | -0.835 | 261.191 | 260 | 325 / 579 | A |
| v3 rep 3 (`s5v3r3-mv49e9xh-a884de`) | 250.558 | 0.285 | 254.296 | 254 | 325 / 575 | A |

Read as: variant 1: the two saves were sent 7695, 7731 and 7719 ms apart (5000 to 5002 ms from A's acknowledgement to B's first key, plus B's typing time and 2.46 s debounce), A first in all three. **Variant 2 (the smallest gap the harness produced): 0.563, 0.162 and 0.231 ms between the two release times** (A released first in all three); the two pages' own request events were 0.635, -0.823 and -0.754 ms apart (a negative value means B's page emitted its event first), because the two clients typed concurrently and both held. **Variant 3: 253.1, 252.7 and 250.6 ms between the releases** (asked 250 ms; the setTimeout and the first release's own await add 0.6 to 3.1 ms), the two request events 0.765, -0.835 and 0.285 ms apart, so in variant 3 the two requests had been issued almost together and held, and the gap is the release gap. Response `updatedAt` values (1 ms resolution) were 249, 260 and 254 ms apart in variant 3 and -1, -1, +1 ms apart in variant 2. **The wire gap and the order in which the server received the two requests were not measured**; "0.16 to 0.56 ms" is the gap between two `route.continue()` calls issued from one Node process. Variant 2 therefore means "released in the same tick, measured 0.16 to 0.56 ms apart", not simultaneous at the server.

**Varied:** the timing of the two saves (5 s in turn, same tick, 250 ms). **Held fixed:** base document (identical in R1 and R2), each client's single marker (` A1` into R1, ` B1` into R2), typing delay (40 ms), one client per resource, A has R1 and B has R2 in every repetition, one plain project, headless Chromium, host to itself, the built server, A opening before B.

### Verdict per variant (against the Task 1 definition, applied PER RESOURCE; raw observation beside it)

The claim under test (owner decision 2026-10-11): "last" = last PROCESSED by the server; a repetition PASSES only if all four stores hold exactly the last-processed client's whole document, parseable, never a mix, and the client shows it after a reload. Applied here per resource: R1 must hold exactly A's document, R2 exactly B's, and neither the other's. The harness `verdict` function was run once per resource per repetition with `requireReload` on (the reloaded client's text must equal the stored document's text). Each resource has exactly one save, so its last processed save is determined by the one response `updatedAt`; the cross-resource order is recorded as evidence only (below) and does not enter the verdict.

| Variant | Verdict | Repetitions | R1 (A's resource): all four stores | R2 (B's resource): all four stores | Raw observation beside the verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 in turn | PASS | 3 of 3 | = `A#1`, `wordCount` 5 | = `B#1`, `wordCount` 5 | each resource has `v-1` only (canonical, "Initial Draft"), holding its own client's document; the other client's marker (`B1` in R1, `A1` in R2) is in no store, no revision, no search hit |
| 2 smallest gap (0.16 to 0.56 ms release gap) | PASS | 3 of 3 | = `A#1`, `wordCount` 5 | = `B#1`, `wordCount` 5 | same |
| 3 250 ms gap (250.6 to 253.1 ms) | PASS | 3 of 3 | = `A#1`, `wordCount` 5 | = `B#1`, `wordCount` 5 | same |

**Per variant: PASS, stable (all 3 repetitions agree, and agree on every field of the table above).** All 9 repetitions: R1 = A's document and R2 = B's document in `content.bin` of the canonical revision, `content.tiptap.json` and `content.txt`, sidecar `wordCount` 5 and sidecar `updatedAt` equal to that resource's own save's response `updatedAt`; neither resource holds the other client's document; each client shows its own document after the reload. **What 3 repetitions per variant bound:** 3 clean repetitions bound a failure rate only loosely (zero failures in 3 leaves an exact one-sided 95% upper bound of about 63%). Nothing here shows that a rare interference between resources cannot happen; it shows that it did not happen in these 9.

**Stated, from those hashes and the per-step snapshots:**

- In every one of the 9 repetitions R1's set of changed files between the fixture and the end is exactly four files: `meta/resource-R1.meta.json`, `resources/R1/content.tiptap.json`, `resources/R1/content.txt`, `revisions/R1/v-1/content.bin`; R2's is the same four with R2. These are the four files a content save writes (read, not run: `revision-core.ts` `updateRevisionInPlace`, `writeRevisionContent`, `syncDerivedResourceContent`, `writeSidecar`). `revisions/<id>/v-1/metadata.json` did not change for either resource, and no file was added to or removed from either resource's paths (`added: []`, `removed: []` in all 9). The two sets are equal after replacing the label (`R1_and_R2_change_sets_equal_after_replacing_label: true` in 9 of 9), and no changed path of either resource lies outside the four (`pathsOutsideTheFourSaveFiles` empty in 9 of 9).
- Opening the resource in the editor changed no file of R1 or R2 (`R1_files_changed_by_opening_or_reload.open: []`, same for R2, 9 of 9), and the reload changed no file at all, resource-level or project-level (`afterSavesToAfterReload` empty in 9 of 9).
- **Variant 1 separates the two saves in time:** in all three repetitions, after A's save and before B typed, R2's files had not changed (`variant1_afterAsSave_R2_changed: []`), R1's four had; after B's save, R1's files had not changed again (`variant1_afterBsSave_R1_changed_since_afterAsSave: []`) and R2's four had. So in variant 1 no file of R1 changed other than through A's save, and none of R2 other than through B's, at the resolution of that snapshot.
- **Limit for variants 2 and 3:** the two saves are 0.16 to 253 ms apart and the snapshots are taken only after both have landed, so the hashes cannot show by time which save wrote which file. What they do show: each resource's four files hold, byte for byte, its own client's document (outcome 1), the changed sets are the same four paths for both resources, and no other path of either resource changed. That is evidence that no file of R1 changed other than through A's save and none of R2 other than through B's in variants 2 and 3, short of the time-separated proof variant 1 gives.
- **Project-level files that changed (listed by path), identical in all 9 repetitions:** `project.json` (changed between the fixture and both-open in 9 of 9, and changed again between both-open and the end, including in variant 1 before B typed, i.e. at or after A's save), `meta/index/diagnostics.json` and `meta/index/inverted.json` (changed by the saves), and `meta/writing-log/2026-10-11.json` (ADDED by the first save: it did not exist before). No other project-level file was added, removed or changed (`meta/backlinks.json`, `meta/index/mentions.json` and the rest did not change). The reload changed none. `.trash` did not exist (projectTrash and projectsFolderTrash both `absent`) in all 9.
- Observation, no cause: the hashes of `content.bin` and `content.tiptap.json` after the save differ from repetition to repetition for the same typed text (for example R1 `content.bin` after: `3f261697`, `9b981ac8`, `42958d07`, ...), while `content.txt` after is identical in all 9 (`b71058e9` for R1, `b310b25e` for R2). The classifier compares each store with the document the client actually sent (equal in every repetition), so this does not affect any verdict. **Hypothesis, not tested:** the editor writes a per-document attribute (an id) that differs between sessions. Experiment that would settle it: parse two saved documents of the same text from two repetitions and diff them; not run (the throwaway folders are removed).
- **Hypothesis, not tested:** that `project.json` is changed by opening and saving (for example a timestamp field in the manifest). Experiment: diff the keys of `project.json` before and after one open and after one save in a throwaway project; not run.

| 1, 2, 3 | after both saves (quiet; quiet wait 1003 to 1006 ms, 2 reads 1000 ms apart) | all four = `A#1`, `wordCount` 5, sidecar `updatedAt` = A's response `updatedAt` | all four = `B#1`, `wordCount` 5, sidecar `updatedAt` = B's response `updatedAt` |

In every repetition `canonicalCount` was 1 for both resources, `v-1` was the only revision directory of each (no auto-backup), no `.tmp-*` entry was left under `revisions/<id>/`, and "stores agree" was true for both.

### Each open editor (outcome 2), text and footer

Each client has only its own resource open, so there is no editor that could hold the other client's text of the same resource. The footer is quoted without the `Words: n | Node: Body |` prefix. `(a)` right after the saves were acknowledged (variant 1: after A's save, B had not typed; after both: after B's save), `(b)` 30 s after the last acknowledgement, no reload, `(c)` after reload. Identical in text across all 9 repetitions: A's editor `BASE alpha bravo charlie A1` at every moment after its save and after the reload, B's editor `BASE alpha bravo charlie B1` after its save, at 30 s and after the reload; B's editor `BASE alpha bravo charlie` (untouched) after A's save in variant 1 only. The footer's autosave label: `Saved · just now` right after a client's own save, `All changes saved · just now`, then `All changes saved · 18s ago` to `25s ago` at 30 s (the two clients' last saves were 7.7 s apart in variant 1 and about 0.2 s or less apart in variants 2 and 3), `All changes saved · not saved yet` after the reload.

**Observation, footer "Today's writing Today: N"** (verbatim part of the footer; the text of the project-wide writing log, which both resources feed): after A's save A showed `Today: 1`; after B's save B showed `Today: 2`; A kept `Today: 1` at 30 s without a reload and showed `Today: 2` after its reload, in variant 1 (3 of 3) and variant 3 (3 of 3). In variant 2 both footers showed `Today: 2` right after the saves (3 of 3). No cause is named. **Hypothesis, not tested:** that the figure is read once after the client's own save and not refreshed when the other client's save lands; experiment: log the timing of each client's `GET /api/project/writing-log` against the second log entry's timestamp (the request logs in the JSON hold both).

### Requests the pages made (outcome 3 and finding (b) input)

Each client sent exactly one `PATCH /api/resource/revision/<id>` carrying a document, 2459 to 2474 ms after its last key (the debounce) in every repetition, status 200, `snapshotCreated: false`, no `writingLog` signal. No other PATCH, no PATCH before the first typing, no PATCH without typing. Variant 1: 2459 to 2462 ms after the last key. In variants 2 and 3 the request event was 2459 to 2474 ms after the last key (2474 ms in variant 2 repetition 1) and the PATCH was held 322 to 336 ms (A) and 323 to 584 ms (B) before the harness released it.

### Notification surfaces (outcome 3), named

Surfaces checked, from the first typing of the repetition to the end, for both clients: every element with `role` `status`, `alert`, `alertdialog` or `dialog` (a MutationObserver, which includes toasts; react-hot-toast's DOM was not inspected), JS dialogs (`dialog` events), console errors and warnings, page errors, failed requests, non-2xx responses, footer text at each step, and the `snapshotCreated` / `writingLog` fields of the PATCH responses. Result, identical in all 9 repetitions: **before the reload mark, the only entry on any surface was the `role=status` text `Loading diagnostics…` (once per client); no toast, no alert, no dialog, no JS dialog, no console message, no page error, no failed request and no non-2xx response.** After the reload mark each client's page recorded: `role=status` `Loading this document…` and `Loading diagnostics…`; console errors `Error fetching projects: TypeError: Failed to fetch` and `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)`; console warnings ``[react-tooltip] Do not set `style.border`. Use `border` prop instead.``; failed requests `net::ERR_ABORTED` on the in-flight `GET /api/...` calls of the old page; and one `GET /api/auth/get-session` answered 404 (the same kinds of entries as in the S1 and S3 records; they sit within about 1 s of the harness's own reload and are reload effects, as the earlier sections state). `snapshotCreated` was false on both PATCH responses in all 9. No `Revision <id> not found` response (404) and no other failed save appeared (see "failed saves"); the FR-37 / POS pointer therefore has nothing to point at in this section.

### Outcome 4, the lost-update shape

Not applicable as such: no client has a stale copy of the resource it saves, because each client has only its own resource open. Established from outcome 1 and the PATCH log: each client's one sent document is the document that its resource's four stores hold afterwards; R1 held no document of B's and R2 none of A's (`holdsTheOtherClientsDocument: false` for both, 9 of 9). The last-key-to-send interval and the markers of every PATCH are in the pasted records.

This is across two resources, so it does not enter a verdict. It is recorded because it is the same kind of evidence S2 will rest on for ONE resource: with releases 0.2 to 0.6 ms apart, the order the server stamped did not always follow the order of release. **Hypothesis, not tested:** that the server handled the two requests concurrently and the interleaving of its two `new Date()` calls decided the stamps. Experiment: S2 (same resource, near-simultaneous, 20 repetitions per variant), or a server-side log of request arrival; not run here.

### Findings (a) to (g), raw observations, NO verdict

- **(a) A stale editor replacing the other device's text on a keystroke:** not exercised. No editor of this scenario holds a stale copy of the resource it saves. R1 held no document of B's and R2 none of A's afterwards.
- **(b) A save sent with no typing:** none. Each client sent exactly one content PATCH, 2459 to 2474 ms after its last key; no PATCH before the first typing; no PATCH after the reload (the reload followed the last stores read).
- **(c) Whether the other device was told anything:** nothing was overwritten. Surfaces named above; before the reload the only entry was `Loading diagnostics…`.
- **(d) Whether overwritten text survives:** nothing was overwritten; each resource has `v-1` only, holding its own client's document; no auto-backup. No overwrite that leaves no recoverable copy was observed in this scenario (it could not occur here, since no resource had two writers).
- **(e) An editor still showing text the server no longer holds:** none. Each editor equalled its resource's stored text at every moment it was read (right after the saves, at 30 s, after the reload).
- **(f) The writing-log effect:** both saves logged `{added 1, deleted 0}`, as expected; the other client's words were not counted as deleted or added. See the table above, including the equal timestamps in variant 2.
- **(g) A failed save on the device the writer believes is last:** none.

### Hypotheses (labelled; none established by this task)

1. The `updatedAt` order across resources not following the release order by 1 ms in variant 2 (above): the experiment is S2 or a server-side arrival log.
2. `project.json` changing at open and at save: diff its keys across one open and one save (not run).
3. The per-repetition difference in the `content.bin` / `content.tiptap.json` hashes for the same typed text: diff two saved documents (not run).
4. The footer's `Today` figure not refreshing for the other resource's save (variants 1 and 3): log the writing-log GET against the entry timestamps (not run).

### What was not exercised by this scenario

- The same resource saved by two clients (S1 to S4, S2).
- More than one resource per client, one client editing both, or each client opening the other's resource (after the reload each client reopened only its own resource; neither client was asked to display the other's resource).
- Sidecar edits, rename, delete or move of either resource while the other saves.
- Different document lengths, long additions, repeated saves per client, more than 3 repetitions per variant.
- Same-tick saves with the harness's smallest gap beyond 0.16 to 0.56 ms; any wire-level or server-side measure of arrival order.
